chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abbas ibn A'mir, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:

I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him to supplicate to Allah that He makes me among those through whom He gives victory to His religion, but he did not answer me, so I became saddened because of that. Yunus said: One of our companions informed me that he had written to him with a similar request and was answered by him, and he wrote at the bottom of the letter: 'May Allah have mercy on you, verily Allah gives victory to His religion via the worst of His creatures.'

key_terms.أَسْفَلِ كِتَابِهِ: at the bottom of the letter
key_terms.بِشَرِّ خَلْقِهِ: via the worst of His creatures

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam not answer Yunus's request to be among those who give victory to God's religion?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi's *Rijal* highlights the concept of *al-istidraj* or divine selection of the humble for victory, contrasting with human expectations of grandeur. The phrase 'worst of His creatures' (*sharr khalqih*) refers to those who may appear insignificant or flawed in worldly eyes but are chosen by Allah to establish His cause, a theme central to Shia understanding of the Imamate and the Mahdi. It serves as a reminder that divine power is not bound by human metrics of status or piety.
